new_public_evidence.source: Douc, Cappe, Moulines, Comparison of Resampling Schemes for Particle Filtering
new_public_evidence.result: Stratified/residual have variance-improvement results over multinomial in the analyzed setting, while systematic has an explicit counterexample and lacks blanket variance dominance.

new_public_evidence.source: Li, Wang, Deng, Liu, Stratification and Optimal Resampling for Sequential Monte Carlo
new_public_evidence.result: Ordered stratification can reduce resampling variance; in one dimension it is connected to optimal transport resampling and minimizes the stated resampling-variance criterion.

new_public_evidence.source: Lee, Whiteley, Variance estimation in the particle filter
new_public_evidence.result: Particle-filter asymptotic variance can be decomposed into time-step contributions estimated from genealogy, and variable particle counts allow approximate asymptotically optimal allocation.

derived_results.claim: A 2-state Feynman-Kac tree with exact initial measure, defensive priority q, post-resampling weight W/(M q), base transition P and potential G has exact Z_5=11.987463336827743. In 30,000-run focused checks, iid, stratified and systematic properly weighted variants under the tested orderings all had mean Zhat within about 1.1 Monte Carlo standard errors of exact, consistent with the conditional unbiasedness proof; this numerical check is not the proof itself.

At T=5 under deliberately alternating low/high-priority ordering, systematic variance was 16.742768 versus 7.987554 stratified and 8.749875 iid: 2.096x stratified and 1.913x iid. The same systematic algorithm under score-sorted ordering had variance 7.316595, so alternating ordering increased its variance by 2.288x. In the 8,000-run T=2..5 grid, systematic/stratified variance under alternating order was 2.544, 2.461, 2.306 and 2.143 respectively.

At T=5 alternating order, stratified retained on average 17.95 unique initial ancestors versus iid 11.18, while reducing mean maximum family fraction from 0.2397 to 0.1462. Systematic retained 18.32 roots but still had much higher estimator variance, showing genealogy diversity alone does not diagnose shared-offset aliasing.

If asymptotic variance is approximated by sum_t A_t/N_t and cost by sum_t k_t N_t=C, Lagrange optimization gives N_t proportional to sqrt(A_t/k_t). With equal costs, N_t proportional to sqrt(A_t). Predictable N_t chosen from past information preserves the fixed-current-count conditional expectation argument.

A 6,000-run pilot around N_t=64 estimated finite-model variance coefficients [245.20,81.69,43.17,54.80,44.22], yielding schedule [111,64,46,52,47] at total descendant budget 320. On an independent 30,000-run validation with ordered stratified priority resampling, variance was 6.284545 versus 7.318577 for uniform [64,64,64,64,64], a 14.13% reduction; reversing the same allocation gave 9.285839, 26.88% above uniform.

engineering_update.scope: Finite-state recursive Feynman-Kac engineering validation plus an analytic square-root allocation rule. Public particle-filter literature supports ordering/stratification and generation-wise variance allocation, but the exact numeric gains reported here are specific to the synthetic model.

negative_or_scope_evidence: Systematic is not declared invalid or generally inferior; the large penalty requires a deliberately bad ordering in this model, while score-sorted systematic was competitive.
Multi-generation total-variance dominance of stratified over iid is not claimed as a theorem from the one-step result.
The allocation pilot used repeated synthetic runs, not a single-run online genealogy estimator; production use needs past-only online A_t estimates.
Predictable particle counts are covered by conditioning on the past; outcome-dependent current-generation stopping is not covered by naive W/(M q).
Environment/tool transitions sampled from a proposal different from the base still require explicit P/Q correction.
No AGI capability or real-agent performance claim follows.
frontier: Replace repeated-run pilot A_t estimates with a single-run/past-only genealogy or ALVar-like variance-contribution proxy, then test predictable square-root N_t adaptation when the high-variance generation moves over time.
Quantify wall-clock value of adaptive N_t under fixed per-generation overhead plus per-particle cost; distinguish variance-per-compute from confirmation-latency gains.
Stress defensive-floor changes and genealogy collapse across 5-20 generations under stratified priority resampling.
If systematic is retained for implementation reasons, require explicit ordering randomization or a conditional-variance test; otherwise keep independent stratified uniforms as the robust default.
Map to real multi-turn agent evaluation only after base/proposal transition likelihoods and high-fidelity label semantics are explicit.
exact_next_action: Implement a drifting 5-generation finite-state model in which the dominant variance contribution moves between generations. From only prior completed generations/runs, estimate per-generation A_t using a genealogy-based or online asymptotic-variance proxy, set the next predictable particle schedule by N_t proportional to sqrt(A_t/k_t), and compare fixed-budget variance plus wall-clock confirmation time against uniform allocation. Preserve independent stratified resampling. In parallel derive the fixed-overhead cost rule: under information gain approximately proportional to M and cost c0+c1 M, quantify the diminishing latency return c0/M and define a stop-buying threshold for extra descendants. Only after that move to agent trajectory semantics.
